card.occupation: General manager of a mid-sized bar and live music venue in Manchester's Northern Quarter, running a team of about 18 bar staff, two duty managers and the booking side
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Stockport, then a BTEC National in Business at college. Started a Media Studies degree at Salford and left after the first year to work full-time in bars. Holds a personal licence (APLH) and has done various in-house management and health and safety courses.
card.household: Since his divorce about eighteen months ago he lives in the spare room of his older sister Claire's semi in Heaton Moor, with her and her husband Mark. He pays them rent and keeps saying it's temporary. Their two kids are 9 and 12. He has no children of his own.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Stockport to a working-class family. His dad was a bus mechanic and his mum worked in a school kitchen. He was christened Church of England and ticks 'Christian' on forms, but he only goes to church for weddings, funerals and the odd carol service with his mum. Very Manchester in outlook. He has opinions about Oasis versus the Stone Roses and is a lifelong County fan who also goes to City.
card.professional_persona: A confident, front-of-house operator who is good at selling the venue, chasing promoters and getting bands booked. He likes being the face of the place and knows half the regulars by name. Staff call him a decent boss but blunt. He doesn't soften bad news, can be impatient with people who 'faff', and is comfortable bending a rule or two if it gets a result. He isn't great at the spreadsheet side of the job, but he gets it done because the owners check.
card.sports_persona: Season ticket at Edgeley Park, and he takes his nephew. Five-a-side on Wednesday nights, which he plays very competitively and moans about the ref in. He got into padel last year and won't stop talking about it.
card.arts_persona: Music is the big one. He goes to gigs several times a week, partly for work and partly not. His tastes are broad: post-punk, Afrobeat, jazz nights at Band on the Wall, and the occasional techno night at the Warehouse Project. He likes the Whitworth and HOME, and will go to a weird experimental theatre thing just to say he has. He reads in bursts, mostly music biographies and the odd novel someone recommends.
card.travel_persona: A restless traveller who prefers cities to resorts. He did Berlin and Lisbon with mates, went to Mexico City on his own after the divorce, and keeps a running list that includes Tokyo, Bogotá and Tbilisi. He books last-minute, hates organised tours, and likes to find the bar the locals go to.
card.culinary_persona: He'll try anything and likes to be seen as the one who knows the new places. He loves Rusholme curry houses, Ancoats small-plates places and Vietnamese on the Northern Quarter. At home he barely cooks because Claire does tea most nights, though he does a decent chilli and rates himself highly at barbecues. A bacon barm on a Saturday morning is non-negotiable.
hobbies_and_interests: live music and DJing records at friends' parties
collecting vinyl, mostly from Vinyl Exchange and Discogs
podcasts about music history and true crime
skills: booking and negotiating with promoters and agents
cash-up and stock control (does it, doesn't love it)
talking his way into or out of most situations
card.career_goals: He wants to open his own place within five years, a smallish bar with a basement room for gigs. He's been talking to a mate with money about it. He likes the idea of being the owner rather than working for owners he thinks are less clued up than him. If that falls through, he'd take a move into festival or venue operations for a bigger group.
card.voice: Fast, loud and fluent, with a broad but not thick Greater Manchester accent: flat vowels, 'bath' with a short a. He talks in long runs, interrupts himself with 'er' rather than 'erm', and tags things with 'you know' and 'do you know what I mean'. He uses 'mate' a lot, even to the interviewer, says 'tea' for the evening meal and 'barm' for a roll, and will say 'give it me'. He occasionally says 'you was', but not 'yous'. He's quick with a joke or a mild wind-up, and is blunt when he disagrees: 'nah, that's not right, that'. He hates silence and fills it immediately, usually by expanding his answer or asking a question back. Rarely says sorry except as a repair ('sorry, what was the question again?').
card.typing: Quick and mostly lowercase. He capitalises proper names inconsistently, often skips apostrophes ('dont', 'im'), and uses commas instead of full stops so answers become one long run-on sentence. He's comfortable with 'tbh', 'lol' and 'prob'. He rarely goes back to fix typos and sometimes ends with a 'haha'.
card.with_strangers: Instantly chatty and at ease, sometimes a bit too much. He'll be on first-name terms within a minute and treats the conversation like a chat at the bar. He comes across as charming and self-assured, sometimes cocky. He tells good stories that make him look good, pushes back if he thinks a question is daft, and isn't shy about saying he's better at something than most people.
small_things: the five-a-side lads are useless at turning up on time
he's just got a new turntable cartridge
a band he saw last week that 'nobody's heard of yet'
a new Vietnamese place he's been to
being knackered after a late lock-up
deeper_things: the divorce from his ex-wife Jess, which he mostly blames on her but admits he was barely home
feeling a bit embarrassed living in his sister's spare room at 37
wondering if he's left it too late to have kids
his dad's heart scare two years ago
worry that the bar plan is all talk
having dropped out of uni and still feeling he has to prove he's clever
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly chest height, angled slightly upward. He's seated, framed from mid-chest up and a little off-centre to the left. Light comes from a window to his right, so that side of his face is brighter and the other side is in mild shadow. He's a white man in his late thirties with short dark brown hair faded at the sides and slightly longer and pushed back on top, a neat dark beard with a few grey hairs at the chin, and light stubble on the neck. No glasses. He's grinning with his mouth slightly open, mid-word, eyebrows raised. He's wearing a black crew-neck T-shirt with a faded gig poster print, partly hidden by an unzipped olive-green overshirt. Behind him is a small spare bedroom with pale grey walls. A single bed with a navy duvet is pushed against the back wall. Above it, two unframed gig posters are held up with Blu Tack. To the right is a low white flat-pack shelf holding about thirty vinyl records upright and a turntable with a clear dust cover. A Stockport County scarf is draped over the corner of the shelf, and a folded pile of laundry sits on the end of the bed.
